fixes.explanation: A city gate! Friend, I love the confidence. But there's no gate anywhere in this verse. Leviticus 14:3 says, “The priest is to go outside the camp to examine him…” The person had been living outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46), so that's where the priest heads. Picture him walking right past the gate without even slowing down, like a man who knows exactly where he's going and has zero interest in the scenic route.

At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting is right, friend! Leviticus 14:11 says the priest presents the person with the offerings “…before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” Look at this guy: he's got two lambs, a ewe lamb, flour and oil, and he's standing right there in front of the LORD. I think that's a lot to carry, and I bet he's grinning anyway. Earlier in the passage he's outside the camp, and now here he is at the Tent of Meeting.

Cleared is right, and it's smart. Leviticus 14:36 says, “The priest must order that the house be cleared before he enters it to examine the mildew…” Then comes the reason: “…so that nothing in the house will become unclean.” So everything comes out before the priest steps in. That's the kind of order I like, friend. Empty the house first, then look at the walls.

problems.problem: The explanation is generic and repetitive, with little of Papa Dorin's personality.
The passage does not say the person was outside the camp eight days ago. It gives steps on the seventh and eighth days, but not that elapsed time.
The priest orders the house cleared, but the text does not say he gives that order to the owner.
Saying the drawer got cleared out contradicts Papa Dorin's backstory. He was taken from it, while his friends and the other contents remained.
